scenario.name: AWS CIRT, Datadog & MITRE — AWS STS GetFederationToken Console Sign-In Bypass & IAM Policy Audit
scenario.overview: Picture a bustling international airport terminal with glowing departure screens, an X-ray security arch, a boarding gate counter, and a commercial passenger airplane parked right outside on the tarmac. Inside the airport terminal, a disguised passenger approaches the boarding gate carrying an altered boarding pass tucked inside an official airline jacket. In this real-world scenario, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the gate agent's station, then smuggles copied records out past the airport security scanner arch in tiny disguised batches. Airfield control tower logs and the boarding-gate manifest counter catch the mismatch when one extra passenger shows up on the jet without a matching ticket purchase. In this scenario (T1550.001, AWS CIRT, Datadog & MITRE, AWS STS GetFederationToken Console Sign-In Bypass & IAM Policy Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: programmatic AKIA Access Key Invocation, then federation SigninToken Exchange, then console Reconnaissance. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Programmatic AKIA Access Key Invocation, then Federation SigninToken Exchange, then Console Reconnaissance, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on CloudTrail Event 200 correlated across the documented kill chain.

specs.value: Remove inline sts:GetFederationToken permissions from IAM Users, migrate from static AKIA keys to IAM Roles Anywhere or SSO, and alert on GetFederationToken calls in CloudTrail.

stages.title: Stage 1: Programmatic AKIA Access Key Invocation of sts:GetFederationToken
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1550.001 - Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token)
stages.description: Inside the airport terminal, a disguised passenger approaches the boarding gate carrying an altered boarding pass tucked inside an official airline jacket. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the gate agent's station while everyday visitors and the gate agent go about their routine. Holding a long-lived IAM User access key (AKIA...), the actor calls sts:GetFederationToken to mint temporary federated credentials (ASIA...) scoped to an inline session policy, logged in AWS CloudTrail (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with EventSource=sts.amazonaws.com, EventName=GetFederationToken, PrincipalUser=ci-deploy-bot , AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=GetFederationToken (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=GetFed so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1550.001 during "Programmatic AKIA Access Key Invocation of sts:GetFederationToken" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). Next, the follow-up artifact jq '.Records[] | select(.eventName=="GetFederationToken")' cloudtrail.json runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , jq '.Records[] | select.eventName=="GetFederationToken"' cloudtrail.json via System / Runt so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1550.001 during "Programmatic AKIA Access Key Invocation of sts:GetFederationToken" , Holding a long-lived IAM User access key , AKIA, the actor calls sts:GetFederationToken to mint temporary federated credentials , ASIA scoped to an inline session policy, logged in AWS CloudTrail while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). stages.title: Stage 2: Federation SigninToken Exchange & Interactive ConsoleLogin Event
stages.subtitle: Lateral Movement (T1078.004 - Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts)
stages.description: At the security arch and gate desk, the scanner reads the legitimate airline logo on the pass and waves the passenger straight down the boarding bridge toward the airplane. Here in Step 2 inside the airport terminal, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the gate agent's station without disturbing the public departures concourse. The actor passes the temporary federated credentials to https://signin.aws.amazon.com/federation?Action=getSigninToken and opens the resulting Console login URL, producing a ConsoleLogin CloudTrail event with userIdentity.type="FederatedUser" and additionalEventData.MFAUsed="No" (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with EventName=ConsoleLogin, IdentityType=FederatedUser , sts:GetFederationToken, MfaStatus=MFAUsed: No so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes jq '.Records[] | select(.eventName=="ConsoleLogin" and .userIdentity.type=="FederatedUser")' cloudtrail.json (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , jq '.Records[] | select.eventName=="ConsoleLogin" and .userIdentity.type=="FederatedUser"' so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1078.004 during "Federation SigninToken Exchange & Interactive ConsoleLogin Event" , The actor passes the temporary federated credentials to https://signin while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact aws guardduty list-findings --detector-id <id> runs (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , aws guardduty list-findings --detector-id <id> against AWS CloudTrail, GCP Cloud Audit, or Mi so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1078.004 during "Federation SigninToken Exchange & Interactive ConsoleLogin Event" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ ConsoleLogin (FederatedUser: ci-deploy-bot/console-broker-session, MFAUsed=No) / ⇠#2 ACK 200) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 AWS STS Endpoint (GetFederationToken)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 AWS Management Console & IAM API).

keySpecs.value: Alert on any CloudTrail ConsoleLogin event where userIdentity.type is FederatedUser and MFAUsed is No, and attach an explicit Deny SCP for sts:GetFederationToken across member accounts.

stages.title: Stage 3: Console Reconnaissance & IAM Policy Version Enumeration Audit
stages.subtitle: Discovery (T1069.003 - Permission Groups Discovery: Cloud Groups)
stages.description: Once aboard the parked passenger airplane on the tarmac, the intruder accesses the cabin service locker and redirects flight cargo manifests before takeoff. In this final step inside the airport terminal, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the airport security scanner arch in tiny disguised batches until the boarding pass scanner & tower log catches the mismatch. Inside the browser session, the federated identity queries IAM policies, S3 buckets, and Secrets Manager secrets, which defenders correlate via the shared principalId (<user_id>:console-broker-session) across CloudTrail management events (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with CorrelatedSessionArn=arn:aws:sts::123456789012:federated-user/console-broker-session, EnumeratedApi=iam:GetAccountAuthorizationDetails, GuardDutyFinding=Policy:IAMUser/RootCredentialUsage so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Next, the follow-up artifact aws iam delete-access-key --user-name ci-deploy-bot --access-key-id AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE runs (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , aws iam delete-access-key --user-name ci-deploy-bot --access-key-id AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE agai so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1069.003 during "Console Reconnaissance & IAM Policy Version Enumeration Audit" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ GetAccountAuthorizationDetails via Federated Console Session / ⇠#3 ACK 200) from Node ③ (#3 AWS STS Endpoint (GetFederationToken)) to Node ④ (#4 AWS Federation Signin Endpoint), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 AWS Management Console & IAM API).
